verdicts.claim: OBJ output from PhotogrammetrySession on iOS is documented ('saved to a USDZ file or a folder (for OBJ output)') with iOS 17 availability, but the only field report is community: passing a directory URL created with `appendingPathComponent("Models/", isDirectory: true)` produced OBJ output; a non-directory URL without .usdz fails with 'Output URL must be specify a .usdz extension file!'. Not confirmed by Apple on iOS specifically.
verdicts.correction: Stands, with one sharpening: Apple does document the directory form for iOS, since the symbol page carries no platform caveat. Declaration (fetched 2026-09-28): `case modelFile(url: URL, detail: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail = .reduced, geometry: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Geometry? = nil)`, iOS 17.0, iPadOS 17.0, Mac Catalyst 15.0, macOS 12.0, not deprecated. The `url` parameter text says: "The request saves a USDZ file if the url ends with .usdz. If url refers to a directory, the request saves an OBJ object and every texture map there." Apple has no iOS-specific statement, iOS sample or WWDC demo of OBJ output. Its own iOS sample writes only Models/model-mobile.usdz. The docs define only two URL forms, so a URL ending in .obj (or any other non-directory, non-.usdz URL) is undefined and should be treated as an error.
verdicts.reasoning: Fetched the Apple doc JSON for modelFile(url:detail:geometry:). The abstract is "An object-creation request saved to a USDZ file or a folder (for OBJ output)." The platforms list starts at iOS 17.0 and has no deprecatedAt. The parameter discussion quoted above makes the choice depend on whether the URL "refers to a directory", with no platform restriction. Nothing in the official material contradicts the claim. The claim's caveat (no iOS-specific confirmation from Apple) is accurate, because the Apple iOS sample only exercises .usdz. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: OBJ output from PhotogrammetrySession on iOS is documented ('saved to a USDZ file or a folder (for OBJ output)') with iOS 17 availability, but the only field report is community: passing a directory URL created with `appendingPathComponent("Models/", isDirectory: true)` produced OBJ output; a non-directory URL without .usdz fails with 'Output URL must be specify a .usdz extension file!'. Not confirmed by Apple on iOS specifically.
verdicts.correction: The core claim stands (OBJ output on iOS is confirmed only by the community, never by Apple), but two details need correcting. (1) The cited forum thread (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/742077, Nov 2023 to Aug 2024) never says which platform or OS version the posters used, and the Aug 2024 fix only says the URL must be a directory, created with `folderURL.appendingPathComponent("Models/", isDirectory: true)`. It does not confirm that OBJ, MTL and textures were written, and no Apple engineer replied. It is not an iOS field report. (2) There is better iOS evidence: VForev/Lidar4Free, a sideloaded iPhone app (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.x per its README), creates `<scan>/Output` with `appendingPathComponent("Output", isDirectory: true)` and `FileManager.createDirectory` before calling `.modelFile(url: output, detail: .reduced)`. It then reads `baked_mesh.obj` plus `baked_mesh.mtl` and textures ("alongside USDA"), and it fails the scan if no OBJ is produced. There is still no iOS 18 report. A macOS project (sygnalinc/Apple-Frameworks-for-TouchDesigner) reports that a URL ending in `.obj` gives `.invalidOutput`, which fits the docs. Mapper rule: create the output directory first, pass a URL whose `hasDirectoryPath` is true (`appendingPathComponent("OBJ", isDirectory: true)` or `appending(path:directoryHint: .isDirectory)`), find the .obj by extension rather than a hard-coded name, and keep the ModelIO fallback (`MDLAsset(url:)` on the USDZ, then `export(to:)` .obj). Verify on the iOS 18.3.2 device in the first Object Capture build.
verdicts.reasoning: Fetched forum thread 742077 twice: it carries RealityKit, AR/VR and Object Capture tags and never names a platform. The error text 'Output URL must be specify a .usdz extension file!' appears there, but the thread could be macOS. GitHub code search found an iOS app (Lidar4Free, LidarFree/Reconstruct/ReconstructionService.swift and LidarFree/Capture/ScanStorage.swift) that relies on on-device directory output. Its comments state "Output goes to a directory URL, not a .usdz file URL. That makes the session write OBJ + MTL + textures (alongside USDA) instead of a single USDZ", and it treats a missing OBJ as a failure. This is working iOS 26 code, so the behaviour exists on iOS. Nothing found for iOS 18. The forum symptom has a likely mechanism: without an explicit directory hint, a file URL for a folder that does not exist yet has no trailing slash, so the session sees a non-.usdz file path. Pre-creating the folder and passing isDirectory: true avoids this. No reports of crashes or macOS-only refusal on iOS. Not refuted, but confidence for iOS 18 stays 'likely' and needs a device check.

open_question_answers.question: Exact value of ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages and PhotogrammetrySession.limits on iPhone 13 Pro Max / iOS 18.3.2 (community says 1000 images on iOS; needs a runtime log).
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: at launch (and when capture starts) log `ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages` (instance property, `@MainActor var maximumNumberOfInputImages: Int { get }`, iOS 17.0+) and `PhotogrammetrySession.limits.maximumNumberOfInputImages` / `.maximumInputImageDimension` (`static let limits: PhotogrammetrySession.Limits`, iOS 17.0+ / macOS 14.0+). Both declarations are verified. Apple gives no number: the docs call Limits 'specific to the device on which the PhotogrammetrySession is run'. The capture session stops at its limit unless isOverCaptureEnabled is true. For PhotogrammetrySession, 'any in excess of the limit will be ignored and an .invalidSample message for the sample will be output'. The only Apple figure is for Mac ('On Mac models with lots of unified memory you can process up to 2000 images', WWDC24 10107). No verifiable source for the community figure of 1000 on iOS was found. Design: read the value at runtime and never hard-code 1000.

open_question_answers.question: Whether PhotogrammetrySession on iOS actually honours the .bounds, .poses, .pointCloud and .modelEntity requests (docs list them as iOS 17+, Apple's iOS sample marks them 'Not supported yet' without requesting them).
open_question_answers.answer: All four requests are listed for iOS 17.0+ with no platform caveat. PhotogrammetrySession.Error has no 'unsupported request' case, so an unsupported request would surface as a requestError at run time, not a compile error. Field evidence: `.bounds` works on iPhone. tristanheilman/react-native-object-capture sends `[modelRequest, .bounds]` from ios/Session/RNPhotogrammetrySession.swift and passes the metric BoundingBox to JS (onDimensions, in metres). No iOS field evidence either way was found for `.poses`, `.pointCloud` or `.modelEntity`. Apple's sample comment 'Not supported yet' only refers to its own switch statement. Architecture: use `.modelFile` plus `.bounds` (both safe). Treat `.poses` and `.pointCloud` as optional extras that log and degrade on requestError. Avoid `.modelEntity` (it keeps the mesh in memory on a 6 GB device); load the USDZ instead. Needs device test: request .poses and .pointCloud once on the 13 Pro Max and log requestComplete or requestError.

open_question_answers.question: Whether OBJ output (directory URL) works on iOS 18 specifically; only forum users report success, no Apple confirmation.
open_question_answers.answer: Documented for iOS 17.0+ ('If url refers to a directory, the request saves an OBJ object and every texture map there'). Community code confirms it on iOS 26 (Lidar4Free: pre-created `Output` directory, `.modelFile(url: output, detail: .reduced)`, reads baked_mesh.obj + .mtl + textures, plus USDA). There is no iOS 18 report, and none of 18.x contradicts it. Needs device test on iOS 18.3.2: pass a pre-created directory URL with hasDirectoryPath == true, then list the directory contents after requestComplete. Plan: issue two modelFile requests (one .usdz file, one directory) or use the ModelIO fallback `MDLAsset(url:)` + `export(to:)` .obj if the directory form fails.

open_question_answers.question: Typical on-device reconstruction time for a 3-pass scan (~200-300 images) on the A15; only qualitative data ('a few minutes', roughly M1-class) exists.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: log wall-clock time from process(requests:) to processingComplete, the image count, requestProgressInfo.estimatedRemainingTime and processingStage, ProcessInfo.thermalState at start and end, and whether the idle timer was disabled. Best available evidence is only qualitative: Apple says 'a few minutes'. An iOS 26 community app notes that on-device 'Reconstruction runs for one to a few minutes'. An independent blog (it-jim, not reachable from this sandbox) reported iPhone 13 Pro Max times close to an M1 Mac mini. Architecture: design the reconstruction screen for 2 to 10 minutes on the A15 with a live progress and ETA display, keep the app foregrounded, and support resume from the checkpoint directory.

open_question_answers.question: Exact declaration/doc availability of Entity.visualBounds(relativeTo:) in the iOS 26 SDK JSON (page not resolvable this session); ModelIO boundingBox is the verified alternative.
open_question_answers.answer: Resolved. It is documented on HasTransform, not directly on Entity (so realitykit/entity/visualbounds... returns 404). Declaration from the current SDK doc JSON: `@MainActor @preconcurrency func visualBounds(recursive: Bool = true, relativeTo referenceEntity: Entity?, excludeInactive: Bool = false) -> BoundingBox`. Available iOS 13.0, iPadOS 13.0, Mac Catalyst 13.0, macOS 10.15, tvOS 26.0, visionOS, not deprecated. Every Entity conforms to HasTransform, so `entity.visualBounds(relativeTo: nil).extents` compiles on iOS 18 and gives metres in world space. Call it on the main actor. MDLAsset(url:).boundingBox remains a valid non-main-actor alternative.

open_question_answers.question: Minimum free storage that triggers insufficientStorage(requiredBytes:) at session start; not documented, log requiredBytes when it happens.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: when `.failed(ObjectCaptureSession.Error.insufficientStorage(requiredBytes:))` or `PhotogrammetrySession.Error.insufficientStorage(requiredBytes:)` occurs, log requiredBytes together with `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage` of the capture folder's volume. Both cases are declared `case insufficientStorage(requiredBytes: Int64)`, iOS 17.0+. There is no documented threshold. For ObjectCaptureSession the docs say only 'The session can't be started since there is not enough storage space in the provided directories'. For PhotogrammetrySession the system 'estimates that it needs requiredBytes of storage'. Architecture: run a pre-flight check before capture (for example, refuse below about 2 to 4 GB free, based on about 2 to 4 MB per HEIC with depth times the maximumNumberOfInputImages read at runtime, plus checkpoint and model), and show requiredBytes in the error copy.
